jobs.name: Daily Delegation Audit
jobs.prompt:
SELF-AUDIT: Scan your session database for the last 24 hours and identify token-waste patterns. Specifically flag:
1. Sessions with >100K input tokens and zero delegate_task calls
2. Sessions with >8 web_search calls and zero delegation
3. Sessions with >15 terminal calls without delegation

For each violation found, analyze what should have been delegated and write a short corrective action to /root/.hermes/pending-fixes.md in this format:
```
## [DATE] - [Session title]
- Violation: [type]
- Root cause: [brief analysis]
- Fix: [specific corrective action]
- Estimated savings: [token/cost estimate]
```

If no violations found, write a single line: "No violations detected on [DATE]."

After writing, append a one-line summary of findings to /root/.hermes/audit-log.md.

DO NOT modify any config or session files. This is read-only analysis + write proposed fixes only.

jobs.name: Daily Knowledge Capture
jobs.prompt:
You are the daily knowledge-capture curator. The script output above (session_digest.py) contains the last 24 hours of real user/assistant conversation from this Hermes system.

Your job: extract DURABLE, factual knowledge worth remembering across sessions, and store it to LanceDB so the agent never has to be re-taught. This directly prevents the user from repeating himself.

STEP 1 — Read the digest above. Identify facts that are:
  • Infrastructure/config truths (server roles, IPs, ports, DB locations, credentials locations, file paths)
  • Tool/system quirks and their workarounds
  • Bug root-causes and fixes discovered
  • User corrections ("it's actually X, not Y") and naming conventions he insists on
  • Verified state that contradicts older beliefs (these are HIGH priority — they supersede stale facts)

DO NOT capture: task progress, "I did X then Y" logs, transient session state, anything stale in 7 days, PR/commit/issue numbers.

STEP 2 — Collect ALL candidate fact-topics first, then dedup-check them in ONE batched call (do NOT run a separate search per fact — that cold-loads the embedding model N times):
  python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/knowledge.py search-batch "topic1|||topic2|||topic3|||..."
The output groups results under '=== QUERY: <topic> ===' headers. A query that prints '(no existing facts — safe to store)' or only low-score (<0.75) hits is NEW — store it. If a near-identical fact exists, skip it. If an existing fact is now WRONG (contradicted by today's verified state), store the corrected version with tag CORRECTION and priority critical — the search layer will surface both, and the newer one wins.

STEP 3 — Store each new fact:
  KNOWLEDGE_TAGS="<comma,tags>" KNOWLEDGE_PRIORITY="<normal|high|critical>" python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/knowledge.py store "<concise declarative fact>"

Write facts as declarative truths, not narrative. "Manifest reads Railway DB, not local postgres" ✓ — "Today I discovered Manifest reads Railway" ✗.

STEP 4 — Keep a one-line audit trail: append "YYYY-MM-DD: captured N facts (topics: ...)" to ~/.hermes/audit-log.md.

Be conservative — 0-5 high-quality facts per day is the target, not volume. If nothing durable happened, store nothing and note "no durable facts" in the audit log. This job runs silently (deliver=local); only your audit-log line records the run.

jobs.name: Memory Honcho Dedup
jobs.prompt:
MEMORY HONCHO DEDUP — run daily. Two-stage safe deletion.

STAGE 0 — READ ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md. Split by '§' into entries. These are canonical.

STAGE 1 — For each entry, call honcho_search(query="<condensed topic>", peer='user', max_tokens=600). If Honcho has a semantically equivalent conclusion (same facts, same detail level), flag it. If Honcho's version is less precise or missing specifics, do NOT flag.

STAGE 2 — Already-flagged entries: if [HONCHO_DUP: YYYY-MM-DD] date ≥3 days ago, REMOVE the entry. Report what was removed. If flagged <3 days ago, leave it.

STAGE 3 — REPORT: if entries were DELETED, write "YYYY-MM-DD: memory dedup removed N entries (topics: ...)" to ~/.hermes/references/audit-log.md. If only flags added, remain silent. If clean, respond "[SILENT]".

SAFETY — An entry is a candidate for removal ONLY if ALL of:
1. Honcho preserves semantically equivalent information at the same detail level
2. The entry does NOT contain hard constraints / rules (MUST, NEVER, hard stop, always gate, do not)
3. The entry does NOT contain specific technical config (IP addresses, version numbers, parameter values, port numbers, procedure steps with exact commands)

If any condition fails, keep the entry. Do NOT use a hardcoded list of protected entries — derive protection from the entry's actual content using the three conditions above.

TOOLS: Use patch(old_string=entire_entry, new_string="...") for flagging; patch(old_string=entire_entry, new_string="") for deletion. Only modify MEMORY.md and audit-log.md.

jobs.name: Memory Dedup Audit
jobs.prompt: Load skill memory-dedup-audit. Execute its STEP 1 and STEP 2 procedures. Report failures only to Cron Jobs channel. If all checks pass on both steps: respond [SILENT] — nothing to report.
